correctness.rationale: Direct expansion of (SN) yields a bijection between star-containing events and transversals of external-witness sets. In two-agent pure complexes these are disjoint opposite-colour stars, giving the exact degree product including leaf and disconnected cases. For three agents, two owner vertices and a complete rectangular owner star make the outside facets correspond bijectively to bipartite graph edges; (SN) is exactly the edge-cover property. #P membership is polynomial verification and hardness cites published Theorem D.1. Added common-colour vertices preserve the count. The standalone checker enumerated 116 two-agent and 145 three-agent instances directly without any mismatch; finite checks supplement the proof.

value.rationale: The capacity is a natural semantic invariant: it counts every facet event that can be designated and made secret at a given local state, across possible valuations, after the established owner-local normalization. The theorem gives all two-agent instances an efficient exact formula and demonstrates that a single additional agent creates #P-complete counting even with only two owner local states and a rigid rectangular owner star. This is a robust structural expressivity/complexity boundary, not a random small invariant or known table recomputation.
